dedupe_keys.name: turkiye 2023 earthquakes tracking public rescue and health needs from 697 313 posts on x

description: This case study analyses posts on the social media platform X during the first nine days after the 6 February 2023 earthquakes in Türkiye to see how people expressed rescue, shelter and public health needs. The authors, researchers at the University of Health Sciences Türkiye, collected 697,313 posts from 6 to 14 February 2023 through the X API v2, measured engagement by hashtag and request type in Python, and used named entity recognition to extract and geocode place names from rescue requests for heat maps; the work is published as an open-access journal article. Coverage is the earthquake-affected provinces of southern Türkiye at post level. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives licence; the post corpus itself is not published. Caveats: the analysis is descriptive, the accuracy of posts was not checked, and users of X are not representative of the affected population. The study found that the first 12 hours were dominated by urgent requests for rescue and heavy machinery, shelter requests such as blankets and tents rose on day two, hygiene items and mobile toilets rose from day four, and requests peaked on days five to seven. Simulation uses: time profiles of relief demand for emergency response and supply models. Related records: the AFAD earthquake catalogue (data-afad-turkiye-earthquake-catalogue) records the events themselves.
